questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
At $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the concentration of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions in $1.00 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ aqueous solution of a weak monobasic acid having acid dissociation constant $\left(K_a\right)=4.00 \times 10^{-11}$ is $\boldsymbol{X} \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{M}$. The value of $\boldsymbol{X}$ is _____ .
Use: Ionic product of water $\left(K_w\right)=1.00 \times 10^{-14}$ at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
questions.solution:
Because concentration of $\mathrm{H}+$ from weak acid is less we need to consider self ionization of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}  also.
 \begin{array}{rl}\mathrm{HX}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightleftharpoons & \mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{X}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \\ 10^{-3}-\mathrm{x} \quad & \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y} \quad \mathrm{x} \\ \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l) \rightleftharpoons & \mathrm{H}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \\ & \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y} \quad \quad \mathrm{y}\end{array}$
Approximation : $\left(10^{-3}-\mathrm{x}\right) \simeq 10^{-3} \begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{x(x+y)}{10^{-3}}=K_a=4 \times 10^{-11}....(1) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad y(x+y)=K w=10^{-14}.....(2)
\end{aligned} \begin{array}{ll}
\text{ Add }(1)+(2) \\
\end{array} \begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & (\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y})^2=5 \times 10^{-14} \\ \Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}=\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=\sqrt{5} \times 10^{-7} \\ \Rightarrow & \mathrm{x}=\sqrt{5}=2.236\end{array}$
Answer 2.23 or 2.24.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The solubility of barium iodate in an aqueous solution prepared by mixing 200 mL of 0.010 M barium nitrate with 100 mL of 0.10 M sodium iodate is $\boldsymbol{X} \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$. The value of $\boldsymbol{X}$ is $\qquad$ .
Use: Solubility product constant $\left(K_{\mathrm{sp}}\right)$ of barium iodate $=1.58 \times 10^{-9}$
questions.solution:
$\left[\mathrm{NaIO}_3\right]=\frac{6}{300}=2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{M}$
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Ba}\left(\mathrm{IO}_3\right)_2(\mathrm{~s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Ba}^{2+}+ & 2 \mathrm{IO}_3^{-} \\ \mathrm{s} \qquad & \left(2 \times 10^{-2}+2 \mathrm{~s}\right)\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}=\left[\mathrm{Ba}^{+2}\right]\left[\mathrm{IO}_3^{-}\right]^2 \\ & 1.58 \times 10^{-9}=\left[\mathrm{Ba}^{+2}\right] \times\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & {\left[\mathrm{Ba}^{+2}\right]=\mathrm{s}=3.95 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{M}} \\ & \mathrm{X}=3.95\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: On decreasing the $pH$ from $7$ to $2$, the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt $( MX )$ of a weak acid $( HX )$ increased from ${10}^{- 4}mol{L}^{- 1}$ to ${10}^{- 3}mol{L}^{- 1}$. The ${pK}_{a}$ of $HX$ is
questions.solution:
At $pH = 7$, i.e., the solubility in water is $S$,

The solubility product, ${K}_{sp} = {S}^{2} - - - - - > 1$

Assume the solubility of sparingly soluble salt is $atpH = 2$

$MX ⇌ {M}^{⊕} + {X}^{⊖}{S}_{1}{S}_{1} - x$

The weak dissociation reaction is as follows,

${X}^{⊖} + {H}^{⊕} ⇌ HX{S}_{1} - x{10}^{- 2}x$

Assume the acid dissociation constant is ${K}_{a}$.

Now, $\dfrac{1}{{K}_{a}} = \dfrac{\left[HX\right]}{\left[{H}^{+}\right]\left[{X}^{-}\right]}$

${K}_{sp} = {S}_{1}\left({S}_{1} - x\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{{K}_{a}} = \dfrac{{S}_{1}}{\left[{H}^{+}\right]{S}_{1} - x}$ assume ${S}_{1} ≃ x$

${S}_{1} - x = \dfrac{{K}_{sp}}{{S}_{1}}$

$\dfrac{1}{{K}_{a}} = \dfrac{{{S}_{1}}^{2}}{\left[{H}^{+}\right]{K}_{sp}} ⇒ {{S}_{1}}^{2} = \dfrac{{10}^{- 2}{K}_{sp}}{{K}_{a}} - - - - - - - > 2$

Now from 1 and 2,

$\dfrac{{{S}_{1}}^{2}}{{S}^{2}} = \dfrac{{10}^{- 2}}{{K}_{a}} ⇒ {K}_{a} = \dfrac{{10}^{- 2} \times {10}^{- 8}}{{10}^{- 6}} ⇒ {K}_{a} = {10}^{- 4} ⇒ {pK}_{a} = 4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Concentration of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ and ${Na}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ in a solution is $1M$ and $1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 2}M$, respectively. Molar solubility of ${PbSO}_{4}$ in the same solution is $X \times {10}^{- Y}M$ (expressed in scientific notation). The value of $Y$ is
[Given: Solubility product of ${PbSO}_{4}\left({K}_{sp}\right) = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 8}$. For ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}, {K}_{a1}$ is very large and ${K}_{a2} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$]

If the numerical value has more than two decimal places, truncate/round-off the value to TWO decimal places.
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases}{H}_{2}{SO}_{4} & \mathop{\to}_{} & {H}^{+} & + & {HSO}_{4}^{2 -} \\ & & 1M & & 1M\end{cases}$ (${K}_{{a}_{1}}$ is very large)

${HSO}_{4}^{-}\overset{}{⇌}{H}^{+} + {SO}_{4}^{2 -}{K}_{{a}_{2}} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$\left[{SO}_{4}^{2 -}\right]$ coming from ${Na}_{2}{SO}_{4} = 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$\dfrac{\left[{SO}_{4}^{2 -}\right]\left[{H}^{+}\right]}{\left[{HSO}_{4}^{-}\right]} = \dfrac{1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 1}{1} > {K}_{{a}_{2}}$

$∴$ Rather than dissociation of ${HSO}_{4}^{-}$ into ${H}^{+}$and ${SO}_{4}^{2 -}$ ions, association between already present ${H}^{+}$ and ${SO}_{4}^{2 -}$ will take place.

Assuming '$x$' $mol / L$ of ${SO}_{4}^{2 -}$ and ${H}^{+}$combines to form ${HSO}_{4}^{-}$

$∴ \left[{SO}_{4}^{2 -}\right] = 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 2} - x$

$\left\begin{array}{ll}\left[{H}^{+}\right] = 1 - x \approx 1 \\ \left[{HSO}_{4}^{-}\right] = 1 + x \approx 1\end{array}\right\}$ (assuming $x < < 1$)

$\dfrac{\left(1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 2} - x\right)1}{1} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$⇒ x = 0 . 6 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$\left[{SO}_{4}^{2 -}\right] = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}M$

${PbSO}_{4}\left(s\right) ⇌ {Pb}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + {SO}_{4}^{2 -}\left(aq\right)$

If solubility of ${PbSO}_{4} = sM$

$∴ \left[{Pb}^{2 +}\right] = s$

$\left[{SO}_{4}^{2 -}\right] = s + 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2} \approx 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$

(assuming $s ≪ 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$)

$∴ s \times 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2} = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 8}$

$s = \dfrac{1 . 6}{1 . 2} \times {10}^{- 6} = 1 . 33 \times {10}^{- 6}$

On comparing with $X \times {10}^{- Y}$

$Y = 6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A solution is prepared by mixing $0 . 01mol$ each of ${H}_{2}{CO}_{3}, {NaHCO}_{3}, {Na}_{2}{CO}_{3}$, and $NaOH$ in $100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of water. $pH$ of the resulting solution is
[Given: ${pK}_{{a}_{1}}$ and ${pK}_{{a}_{2}}$ of ${H}_{2}{CO}_{3}$ are $6 . 37$ and $10 . 32$, respectively. $log2 = 0 . 30$]
questions.solution:
First acid base reaction between ${H}_{2}{CO}_{3}$ and $NaOH$ takes place.

$\mathop{{H}_{2}{CO}_{3}}_{0 . 01mole} + \mathop{NaOH}_{0 . 01mole} ⟶ \mathop{\mathop{{NaHCO}_{3}}_{-}}_{0 . 01mole} + {H}_{2}O$

After the acid base reaction, we have $0 . 01mole{Na}_{2}{CO}_{3}$ and $0 . 02$ moles of ${NaHCO}_{3}$. Here, This will form an acidic buffer of ${NaHCO}_{3}$ and ${Na}_{2}{CO}_{3}$.

$∴ pH = {pK}_{{a}_{2}} + log\dfrac{\left[Salt\right]}{\left[Acid\right]}$

$= 10 . 32 + log\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{0 . 01}{0 . 1}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{0 . 02}{0 . 1}\right)}$

$= 10 . 32 + log\dfrac{1}{2}$

$= 10 . 32 - log2$

$= 10 . 32 - 0 . 3$

$= 10 . 02$

$∴ pH = 10 . 02$

questions.q:
For the following reaction, the equilibrium constant ${K}_{e}$ at $298K$ is $1.6 \times {10}^{17} .$
$F{e}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + {S}^{2 -}\left(aq\right) ⇌ FeS\left(s\right)$
When equal volumes of $0.06MF{e}^{2 +}\left(aq\right)$ and $0.2M{S}^{2 -}\left(aq\right)$ solutions are mixed, the equilibrium concentration of $F{e}^{2 +}\left(aq\right)$ is found to be $Y \times {10}^{- 17}M .$ The value of $Y$ is __________
questions.solution:
${\text{Fe}}^{\text{2+}} + {\text{S}}^{\text{2-}} ⇌ \text{Fe}{\text{S}}_{( \text{s} )}$ ..... ${\text{K}}_{\text{c}} = 1.6 \times {10}^{17}$
$\text{t} = 0$ : $0.03\text{M}\left(0.1\text{M}\right)$
$\text{t} = \text{t;}\left(0.03 - \text{H}\right)\left(0.1\text{H}\right)$
Since ${\text{K}}_{\text{c}} > > 1,$
$n ≃ 0.03$
$∴ [ {\text{S}}^{\text{2-}} ] = 0.1 - 0.031 = 0.07\text{M}$
${\text{K}}_{\text{c}} = \left[{\text{Fe}}^{2 +}\right]\left[{\text{S}}^{\text{2-}}\right] = \dfrac{1}{1.6 \times {10}^{17}}$
$\left[{\text{Fe}}^{2 +}\right] = \dfrac{1}{1.6 \times 0.07} \times {10}^{- 17}$
$\text{y} = \dfrac{1}{1.6 \times 0.07} ≃ 8.93$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The dilution processes of different aqueous solutions with water are given in LIST-I. The effects of dilution of the solutions on $[ {H}^{+} ]$ are given in LIST-II.
(Note: The degree of dissociation $\left(\alpha\right)$ of a weak acid and a weak base is $< < 1;$ the degree of hydrolysis of salt is $< < 1; [ {H}^{+} ]$ represents the concentration of ${H}^{+}$ ions)
LIST –I LIST -II
A) $10mLof0 . 1MNaOH + 20mLof0 .1 M$acetic acid diluted to $60mL$. P) The value of $[ {H}^{+} ]$ does not change on dilution.
B) $20mLof0 . 1MNaOH + 20mLof0 . 1M$ acetic acid diluted to $80mL$. Q) The value of ${\text{[H}}^{+} ]$ changes to half of its initial value on dilution.
C) $20mLof0 .1 MHCl + 20mLof0 .1 M$ammonia solution diluted to $80mL$. R) The value of $[ {H}^{+} ]$ changes to two times its initial value on dilution.
D) $10mL$ saturated solution of $Ni{\left(OH\right)}_{2}$ in equilibrium with excess of solid $Ni{\left(OH\right)}_{2}$ is diluted to $20mL$ (solid $Ni{\left(OH\right)}_{2}$ is still present after dilution). S) The value of $[ {H}^{+} ]$ changes to $\sqrt{}$ times its initial value on dilution.
T) The value of $[ {H}^{+} ]$ changes to $\sqrt{2}$ times its initial value on dilution.

Match each process given in LIST-I with one or more effect(s) in LIST-II. The correct option is
questions.solution:
$( A )$

$pH = pKa ⇒ \left[{H}^{+}\right] will not change on dilution.
$( B )$

\left[{OH}^{-}\right]$ = \sqrt{{K}_{H}C} = \sqrt{$\left(\dfrac{{k}_{w}}{{k}_{a}}C\right)$}$
${$\left[{H}^{+}\right]}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{w}{k}_{a}}{C}}$
$\dfrac{{\left[{H}^{+}\right]$}_{2}}{{$\left[{H}^{+}\right]}_{1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{C}_{1}}{{C}_{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{0 .05}{0 .025}}$= \sqrt{2}$
$( C )$

\left[{H}^{+}\right] = \sqrt{{K}_{H}C}$
$\dfrac{{\left[{H}^{+}\right]}_{2}}{{\left[{H}^{+}\right]}_{1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$( D )$ Because of dilution, the solubility does not change. So, $\left[{H}^{+}\right]$ = constant$.$

questions.q:
When 100 mL of 1.0 M HCl was mixed with 100 mL of 1.0 M NaOH in an insulated beaker at constant pressure, a temperature increase of ${5.7}^{o}C$ was measured for the beaker and its contents (Expt.1). Because the enthalpy of neutralization of a strong acid with a strong base is a constant $( - 57.0kJmo{l}^{- 1} )$ , this experiment could be used to measure the calorimeter constant. In a second experiment (Expt. 2), 100 mL of 2.0 M acetic acid $( {K}_{a} = 2.0 \times {10}^{- 5} )$ was mixed with 100 mL of 1.0 M NaOH (under identical conditions to Expt. 1) where a temperature rise of ${5.6}^{o}C$ was measured. (Consider heat capacity of all solutions as $4.2J{g}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$ and density of all solutions as $1.0gm{L}^{- 1}$ )
The pH of the solution after Expt. 2 is
questions.solution:
Final solution contain 0.1 mole of $C{H}_{3}COOH$ and $C{H}_{3}COONa$ each.
Hence it is a buffer solution.
$pH = p{K}_{a} + log\dfrac{[ C{H}_{3}CO{O}^{-} ]}{[ C{H}_{3}COOH ]}$
$= 5 - log2 + log\dfrac{0.1}{0.1} = 4.7$

${\text{CH}_{3} {\text{COOCH}_{3} + {\text{H}_{2} \text{O} \overset{\left[{\text{H}}^{+}\right]}{\to} {\text{CH}_{3} \text{COOH} + {\text{CH}_{3} \text{OH ​}$
$\text{Rate Law} ⇒ \text{k} \left[\text{MA}\right] \left[{\text{H}}^{+}\right]$ (as water is present in large excess)

$\dfrac{\text{I}}{\text{II}} = \sqrt{{\text{K}}_{\text{a}}} = \dfrac{1}{1 0 0} = 1 {0}^{- 2}$
${\text{K}}_{\text{a}} = 1 \times 1 {0}^{- 4}$.

questions.q: In $1 \mathrm{~L}$ saturated solution of $\mathrm{AgCl}\left[K_{\mathrm{sp}} \mathrm{AgCl}=1.6 \times 10^{-10}\right], 0.1$ mole of $\mathrm{CuCl}\left[K_{\mathrm{sp}}(\mathrm{CuCl})=1.0 \times 10^{-6}\right]$ is added. The resultant concentration of $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$in the solution is $1.6 \times 10^{-x}$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
It is a case of simultaneous solubility of salts with a common ion. Here solubility product of $\mathrm{CuCl}$ is much greater than that of $\mathrm{AgCl}$, it can be assumed that $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$in solution comes mainly from $\mathrm{CuCl}$.

\Rightarrow \quad$\left[\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\right]=\sqrt{K_{s p}(\mathrm{CuCl})}=$10^{-3} $\mathrm{M}$Now for $\mathrm{AgCl}: K_{s p}=1.6 \times 10^{-10}=\left[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\right]\left[\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\right]=\left[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\right] \times 10^{-3} \Rightarrow\left[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\right]=1.6 \times 10^{-7}$

questions.q: $2.5 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{M}$ weak monoacidic base $\left(K_b=1 \times 10^{-12}\right.$ at $\left.25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$ is titrated with $\frac{2}{15} \mathrm{M} \mathrm{HCl}$ in water at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The concentration of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$at equivalence point is $\left(K_w=1 \times 10^{-14}\right.$ at $\left.25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$
questions.solution:
Weak monoacidic base, e.g. $\mathrm{BOH}$ is neutralised.

$\mathrm{BOH}+\mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{BCl}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ At equivalence point all $\mathrm{BOH}$ gets converted into salt and remember! the concentration of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$(or $\mathrm{pH}$ of solution) is due to hydrolysis of resultant salt ($\mathrm{BCl} , cationic hydrolysis here)

\underset{\mathrm{C}(1-h)}{\mathrm{B}^{+}}+ \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \underset{\mathrm{Ch}$}{\rightleftharpoons} $\mathrm{OH}+$\underset{$\mathrm{Ch}}{\mathrm{H}^{+}}$Volume of $\mathrm{HCl}$ used up,

V_a=$\frac{N_b V_b}{N_a}=\frac{2.5 \times 2 \times 15}{2 \times 5}=7.5 \mathrm{ mL}$ Concentration of salt,

$\begin{aligned}
{[\mathrm{BCl}]$}$& =\frac{\text{ Concentration$ of $base }}{\text{ Total volume }}=\frac{2 \times 25}{5(7.5+2.5)}=\frac{1}{10}=0.1 \\
K_h & =\frac{C h^2}{1-h}=\frac{K_w}{K_b}
\end{aligned}

(h$ should be estimated whether that can be neglected or not) on calculating $h=0.27$ (significant, not negligible)

 $\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=$ C h=0.1 \times 0.27=2.7 \times 10^{-2} $\mathrm{M}$

When $\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]$ is asked to calculate in connection with neutralisation, it
Should be calculated:
Before neutralisation Using Oslwald's dilution law
During neutralisation $\quad$ Considering buffer solution
Half neutralisation $\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{p}  K_a$ and $\mathrm{p}$  K_b$
At the end of neutralisation $\quad$ Considering hydrolysis of salt$

questions.explanation:

$$
At equivalence point all $\mathrm{BOH}$ gets converted into salt and remember! the concentration of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$(or $\mathrm{pH}$ of solution) is due to hydrolysis of resultant salt ( $\mathrm{BCl}$, cationic hydrolysis here)

$$
Volume of $\mathrm{HCl}$ used up,
$$
V_a=\frac{N_b V_b}{N_a}=\frac{2.5 \times 2 \times 15}{2 \times 5}=7.5 \mathrm{~mL}

Concentration of salt,
$$
\begin{aligned}

K_h & =\frac{C h^2}{1-h}=\frac{K_w}{K_b}
\end{aligned}
$$
( $h$ should be estimated whether that can be neglected or not) on calculating $h=0.27$ (significant, not negligible)
$$
\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=C h=0.1 \times 0.27=2.7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{M}
$$

Should be calculated:
